title: Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl)
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400) is mandated for Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) because its specific strength (290 kN·m/kg) outperforms 4340 steel by 55% and 7075 aluminum by 35% at temperatures up to 400°C. The duplex alpha+beta microstructure provides damage tolerance against high-cycle vibration spectra typical of airframe structures. Its fatigue crack growth rate (da/dN ~2×10^-8 m/cycle at ΔK=20 MPa√m) enables safe-life design for Low-pressure turbine blade, gamma-TiAl intermetallic. This rationale is driven by low-pressure turbine blade, gamma-tial intermetallic and service environment demands.

faq.q: What fatigue life can Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) achieve under flight load spectra?
faq.a: Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) designed to safe-life criteria per MIL-STD-1530 demonstrates minimum 10⁵ flight cycles for lowpressure turbine blade at 75% of yield strength. The fatigue crack growth rate in Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V follows da/dN = 2.2×10⁻⁸ (ΔK)³·² m/cycle in air, with a threshold ΔKth of approximately 5.5 MPa√m. Crack growth predictions use AFGROW or NASGRO with validated material data.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) orders?
faq.a: Standard lead time for Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) is 15-25 business days depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders (3-5 working days) are available for prototype evaluation. Sample evaluation (1-5 units) can be expedited to 5-7 business days. Volume pricing is available for production quantities above 100 units.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl)?
faq.a: Each Titanium LPT Blade (Gamma-TiAl) shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for lowpressure turbine blade.
